# Docker Sandbox (sbx)

Run a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or a plain shell) in an isolated microVM
with the app's toolchain installed, a dev-only `.env`, an egress allowlist, and
real credentials kept on the host behind the sbx proxy.

| Piece | What it controls | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Image `rr7-sbx` (shared by every app) | What is installed: Node, sqitch, psql, bao, Claude Code, Codex, Playwright + Chromium, bun, zsh, fzf, git-delta | rr7-starter's `devcontainer-template/sbx/Dockerfile`, pins in `versions.json` |
| Kit (this app) | Dev `.env`, start hook, network allowlist, agent instructions | `.sbx/kit/spec.yaml`, generated from `.sbx/project.json` |

## Quick start

```sh
bash <rr7-starter checkout>/scripts/sbx-image.sh   # once, and after a version bump
./.sbx/run.sh                 # Claude Code in sandbox "panel", app on http://localhost:5195
./.sbx/run.sh codex           # sandbox "panel-codex"
./.sbx/run.sh shell           # sandbox "panel-shell", no port
./.sbx/run.sh claude --clone  # anything after the agent goes to `sbx run`
```

`run.sh` checks the image is loaded, clones this repo to `~/sbx/panel` if
needed (with `origin` pointing at your real remote), refuses to start if that
checkout has a `.env` it didn't write, and runs `sbx run` with the kit, name and
port. Running it again re-attaches. `SBX_HOME`, `SBX_IMAGE` and `SBX_NAME`
override the defaults.

**Why a separate checkout:** a sandbox can read every file in its workspace,
including untracked ones such as `.env` (a `:ro` mount only blocks writes). A
fresh clone holds committed files only, and it keeps the sandbox's Linux
`node_modules` out of your own checkout.

On every start the kit's hook runs before the agent attaches: it writes the dev
`.env` if missing and runs `npm ci` if `node_modules` is missing, then starts
Postgres (`npm run db:local:up`) and migrates (`npm run db:deploy`). Log:
`/var/log/sbx-kit-startup.log` inside the sandbox.

## Credentials

**Agent sign-in.** With no `anthropic`/`openai` secret stored, `/login` runs the
agent's normal OAuth flow inside the VM. The session survives stop/start and
re-attaching, but a new sandbox starts logged out.

**Provider keys and tokens** are only needed when the sandbox must call the real
service (the dev `.env` uses console transports). Add them on the host with
`.sbx/secret.sh`, which works whether or not the sandbox exists or is running:

```sh
# GitLab token so the agent can push branches and open MRs over HTTPS
./.sbx/secret.sh --host gitlab.com --env GITLAB_TOKEN --command 'glab auth token'

# A provider key read from OpenBao (or any CLI that prints it) at use time
./.sbx/secret.sh --host api.example.com --env EXAMPLE_API_KEY \
  --command 'bao kv get -mount=kv -field=example_api_key apps/panel/staging'

./.sbx/secret.sh --sandbox panel-codex ...   # another sandbox of this app
sbx secret ls                                   # what is registered
sbx secret rm --host api.example.com            # remove one
```

The sandbox only ever sees a placeholder; the proxy swaps in the real value on
requests to `--host`. Plain `sbx secret set-custom` also works, but only for
sandboxes created after it: the placeholder variable is fixed at creation.
`secret.sh` registers the secret and also writes the variable into a running
sandbox, so nothing has to be recreated.

## Day to day

```sh
sbx run --name <name>                       # re-attach to the agent
sbx exec -it <name> bash                    # a shell alongside it
sbx ports <name> --publish 127.0.0.1:5195:5195   # forgot the port
sbx policy log                              # what egress was denied
sbx policy allow network --sandbox <name> <host>
sbx stop <name>   /   sbx rm <name>
sbx kit validate ./.sbx/kit                 # after a re-render
```

**Editing.** In direct mode (the default) the workspace is a bind mount: open
`~/sbx/panel` in your editor and changes flow both ways. For terminals and
extensions inside the VM, or in clone mode, run `sbx setup ssh` once and connect
with VS Code Remote-SSH to `<name>.sbx`. Only enable SSH agent forwarding for a
sandbox that must push over SSH; it exposes every key loaded in your agent.

**Clone mode** (`--clone`): the sandbox works on its own clone. Get its work out
with `git fetch sandbox-<name>`, and pull host changes in from inside with
`git fetch /run/sandbox/source main`.

## Notes

- This file, `kit/spec.yaml`, `run.sh` and `secret.sh` are generated by
  rr7-starter's `scripts/devcontainer-sync.mjs`. Edit the templates under
  `devcontainer-template/sbx/` (shared) or `.sbx/project.json` (this app), then
  re-run it.
- To update Node or the agents: edit rr7-starter's `devcontainer-template/versions.json`,
  rerun `scripts/sbx-image.sh`, then recreate sandboxes (existing ones keep their image).
  `PUSH=<registry>/rr7-sbx bash scripts/sbx-image.sh` also pushes it.
- Vite listens on all interfaces only when `DEVCONTAINER=true`, which the kit sets;
  otherwise the published port reaches nothing.
- Network: sbx's default policy plus the hosts in `kit/spec.yaml`, which mirror
  `project.json`'s `firewall.domains`.
- `~/.claude` is not mounted into sandboxes; only project-level config applies.
